study.title: Electro-Acupuncture Decreases Postoperative Pain and Improves Recovery in Patients Undergoing a Supratentorial Craniotomy
study.comparator_class: No treatment / usual care; no needles, not sham
study.independence: Distinct supplied publication. Same center and several investigators/acupoints as cited An2010a/b and Yang2012; paper calls them previous studies, but no recruitment dates or registry identifier establishes participant nonoverlap. Do not assume duplicate solely from authorship; unresolved author check.

final.Timepoint/window: Reported total during postoperative PCIA course, apparently through 48 h; exact clock not explicit
final.Other analysis eligibility: Hold quantitative fentanyl pooling pending clarification of units, delivery accounting and interval; retain printed raw summaries
final.Source-QC issue: Seven randomized exclusions; no exact24h. Dose accounting inconsistent with no-basal10µg/kg/100mL and reported effective bolus counts. Printed NS does not reconcile with mean/SD/n (independent-groups t approximately2.54). Do not silently correct mg to µg or alter decimal place.

field_checks.source_location: PDF p5 final paragraph; methods p3; Table2 p6
field_checks.evidence: Printed postoperative total fentanyl is 0.67±0.09 versus0.73±0.12 mg, n41/40. The paper says no difference. The stated weight-dependent concentration and effective1-mL bolus counts do not explain the printed totals; the stated no-difference claim also conflicts with a conventional t-test of these mean/SD/n.
